location: New Delhi (Dyal Singh College, Vijay Nagar; families in TN, Karnataka, Odisha)
narrative: On 12-13 March 2026, ten students and labour-rights activists — including Delhi University student Ilakkiya, labour activist Shiv Kumar, BSCEM members Abinash (21) and Akshay (24), and former BSCEM president Gurkirat — were allegedly picked up and detained without due process by Delhi Police personnel in plain clothes, identified by detainees as Special Cell. Pickups began outside Dyal Singh College, where Ilakkiya and Shiv Kumar had gone to meet a professor about a 31 March programme commemorating Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru (Anti-Imperialism Week, organised by the Forum Against Corporatisation and Militarisation), and continued at a Vijay Nagar room where friends had assembled. Detainees allege assault, denial of food to Ilakkiya on the first day, seizure of phones, a diary, Metro card and money without documentation, and being told to cancel the programme. Nine of the ten were released barely 12 hours before the Delhi High Court heard habeas corpus petitions in an unusual Sunday sitting (the tenth, Abinash, says he was released around 1 am on 15 March); the court directed preservation of CCTV footage of the pickup locations. In August 2026, those released and their families reported continuing harassment: repeated police visits every 7-10 days to Gurkirat's parents' home in Shivaji Enclave with notices in old cases, and home visits to families in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Odisha.
status_detail: On 19 May 2026 Delhi Police told the Delhi High Court an inquiry has been initiated into the alleged illegal detention and torture; came after the court's rebuke. CCTV preservation order from March 2026 standing. Inquiry outcome pending as of 2026-09-26.

surveillance.summary: Post-release tracking and intimidation alleged: police personnel allegedly visiting families across states months after release, questioning parents, serving notices in old cases including defamation.

entries.allegation: During detention, Shiv Kumar alleges officers threatened to kill the detainees; he reported sleeplessness and nervousness after release.

Gurkirat (ex-BSCEM president, now at Panjab University) alleges Delhi Police personnel visit her parents' Shivaji Enclave home every 7-10 days for several months, asking her whereabouts and serving notices in old cases including defamation cases.
Families of the students in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Odisha report repeated home visits, questioning of parents and relatives, and surveillance months to years after the March 2026 detentions.
